Read this first

This is an educational reference built from two harm-reduction handbooks about peptides and anabolic-androgenic steroids. It exists to explain how these compounds work and interact, not to encourage or instruct their use.

These substances carry real and sometimes serious health risks. Most are not approved for human consumption and many are controlled substances. Nothing here is medical or legal advice. Do not take anything without the supervision of a qualified medical professional.

If you are under 18, this content isn't for you.

Bloodwork Analyzer

Enter, paste or upload your results. The app flags each value against the handbook's healthy ranges, explains what moves it, and surfaces the handbook's protective measures for your goal. It flags and educates. It does not prescribe drug doses.

This is not a diagnosis and not a substitute for a clinician reading your labs. Anything flagged here, especially high hematocrit, liver enzymes or blood pressure, needs a real doctor. Nothing is stored; values stay in your browser.
Women's ranges applied. Testosterone, estradiol, SHBG, LH/FSH, hematocrit, hemoglobin, RBC and creatinine are being judged against female reference ranges. Female hormone levels also shift a lot across the menstrual cycle and with contraception, so one reading is a snapshot, interpret trends with a doctor. For women, the enhancement concern is less about recovery/PCT and more about keeping androgen-sensitive markers in check and watching for virilization.

Compound dosing

Peptide Reconstitution

How much liquid to draw for a target dose after mixing a powder vial with bacteriostatic water.

Dose & Unit Converter

Convert a mass between units, and split a weekly dose into per-injection amounts.
IU conversions are substance-specific (e.g. HGH ≈ 3 IU per mg) and aren't included here.

Weekly → Per-Injection

Split a weekly dose across injections (e.g. long esters once or twice a week).
Double-check every calculation yourself before acting on it. Dosing errors with these compounds are dangerous.

Training Planner

Set your experience, training days per week and goal. You'll get a weekly schedule with built-in rest days, sets and reps. Log your lifts for auto-progression and a recovery map of what's trained vs. ready. Not coaching advice for your specific situation.

Vitals & Blood Pressure

Know the Signs

The adverse events worth recognising early, what it is, why it happens, and what to do. Red items are emergencies. Awareness is the point: the leading cause of harm here is not knowing what a warning sign looks like.

Supplements

Everything you take, in one place. Supplements and vitamins for health and performance, plus the enhanced compounds, gear and peptides, for reference.

OTC Supplements

Even over-the-counter supplements can help, or quietly work against, your cycle, your goals and your bloodwork. Green is complementary; amber is worth caution.

Alcohol & Other Substances

How everyday recreational substances interact with your training, your recovery and, especially, a cycle. This is harm-reduction information, not encouragement: for most of these, the safest amount on cycle is none. Red = high-risk combination.

Considering enhancement?

An honest, no-hype look before you decide. The leading cause of harm in this space is a lack of knowledge, so start here.
